commands.description: List workspaces visible to the current profile.
Show workspace metadata, channels, and active human and agent participants. --workspace accepts an id, URL slug, or unambiguous name.

List active workspace participants, including people, server-managed agents, and external CLI agents. Add --compact for copyable tab-separated ids; pass an agent's bare UUID from its agent:<uuid> participant id to agent retire.

commands.command: craken workspace activity --workspace WORKSPACE [--limit N] [--surfaces SURFACES]

commands.description: Listen for new human messages as NDJSON. By default, select channels, resume the saved scan position (or start at the current head), and reconnect with bounded retries. --include-dm includes only DMs involving this identity. --mentions-me matches visible channel text using this participant’s aliases; included DMs need no mention. User aliases include display name/email and @everyone; agents use only their own name. --sender-kind agent|system overrides the human default. Stable ids allow deduplication after a crash; output is not a processing acknowledgement.

commands.command: craken channel create --workspace WORKSPACE --name NAME [--purpose PURPOSE]
commands.description: Create a workspace channel and join it using the approving user’s current workspace authority.

commands.command: craken channel update --workspace WORKSPACE --channel CHANNEL [--name NAME] [--purpose PURPOSE]
craken file get --workspace WORKSPACE --file FILE --output PATH
commands.description: Read file content to a path.

commands.command: craken file update-content --workspace WORKSPACE --file FILE --content-file PATH
craken wiki save --workspace WORKSPACE --title TITLE (--content TEXT | --content-file PATH) [--existing-title TITLE] [--base-version VERSION]
commands.description: Create or update a wiki page. Choose --content or --content-file (use - for stdin), not both. Read an existing page first and pass its latestVersionNumber as --base-version; a stale or omitted version returns 409. --existing-title selects the update route and identifies the current title; --title can rename it.
examples: craken wiki save --workspace W --title New --content "A new page"
